quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to survive an accident?

options.text: Ask others about how to ride more safely.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when you ride?

options.text: Any gear that helps to protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps to protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be riding in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is happening behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be riding in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly alongside a vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver cannot see you. The vehicle could also block your escape route if you need to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, what should you remember about motorcycles?

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to cause any problems.
Have blind spots that require head checks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require head checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should proper motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever makes you most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for proper protection while riding.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Encourage them to take roads that are not crowded.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride after drinking. Do whatever you can to stop them, including taking their keys. Help arrange a safe way for them to get home.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, which of these should you NOT look at?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: What type of material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the greatest protection for motorcyclists. Wear clothing made of leather that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle tailgaters?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate faster and increases the danger.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the best traction on dry pavement. Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers all reduce traction.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Regular maintenance checks should be part of your routine care.

questions.question: Which color should you wear to be more visible?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Bright clothing makes you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
Are not helpful because you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Always use your mirrors before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel.
Set a limit beforehand so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about your riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: For the best protection, make sure your helmet:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is securely fastened is the single most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and allow them to get in front of you. Riding faster may increase danger.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to provide better grip on the handlebars.
Not be worn because they make it harder to work the controls.
Be worn only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to provide better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do about lane position?

options.text: Stay in the same spot in the lane at all times.
Weave around the lane to keep other drivers away.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where you position yourself in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position in the lane as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What do you NOT need to check before every ride?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check the spokes for damage, the tire tread, and all lights. You do not need to check the seat fabric.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all motorcycles are the same.
Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and gear shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, check where the controls are and learn the gear pattern. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes first.
